results.title: Omnigraph | Open Source Alternative to Neo4j, TigerGraph
results.content:
Omnigraph is a strong option for teams building agent memory, company knowledge graphs, context graphs or versioned research data, who want an alternative to Neo4j, TigerGraph or Amazon Neptune without running a separate database cluster. Its branching model, open storage format and combined graph and vector search make it especially well suited to AI applications where context has to be both reliable and reviewable.

results.title: Omnigraph | Modern Relay
results.content:
### What database should I use for AI agent memory?

+

One your agents can write to safely and you can audit. In Omnigraph each agent writes on its own branch, the schema is enforced on every write, Cedar policies run inside the engine, and changes reach main only through a merge you can diff first. Every version stays readable, so you can see what an agent knew and when.

### Is Omnigraph a Neo4j alternative?

+

For agent workloads, yes. Neo4j is a mature graph database. Omnigraph is MIT-licensed, keeps the graph as open files in storage you own, and is built around what agents need: git-style branches and merges, a typed schema checked on every write, built-in vector and full-text search, and in-engine policy.

### Does Omnigraph work with MCP?

+ [...] +

Usually both. A vector database finds text similar to a question; a graph database follows how people, projects and decisions connect. Omnigraph does both in one query: vector, keyword and hybrid ranking over the same typed nodes you traverse, so there are no two stores to keep in sync.

### Can I use Omnigraph for GraphRAG?

+

Yes. Store documents, chunks and the entities they mention as typed nodes and edges, with embeddings on the nodes. One query ranks chunks by vector, keyword or hybrid similarity and traverses to the related entities and sources, so the context you give the model comes with its connections.
